description: Self-eval fixture: 6 scripted multi-session users exercising fact evolution, multi-hop, implicit facts, corrections, opinion arcs, retraction, preferences, and noise resistance. Ingested in order by scripts/selfeval.py.

conversations.comment: Fact evolution (job change), multi-hop (dog name <-> city), implicit fact (pet from 'walking Biscuit')

messages.content: Hey! Quick question about TypeScript config. For context I'm a backend engineer at Stripe, we use tsconfig strict mode everywhere.
Happy to help! Strict mode at Stripe makes sense. What's the question?
Sorry, got distracted — was walking Biscuit this morning and he chewed through his leash, had to improvise. Anyway: how do I get noImplicitAny to play nice with legacy JS imports?
Ha, hope Biscuit is okay! For legacy JS imports you can use allowJs with checkJs disabled, or add declaration stubs.
I'm planning a move soon and weighing neighborhoods. We ended up choosing Denver — signing the lease next week. Any tips for finding dog-friendly apartments?
Congrats on Denver! For dog-friendly places, check the pet deposit terms and nearby parks — Denver has great ones like Cheesman Park.
Big news — I just started at Notion this week as a product manager! Switching from engineering to PM has been a whirlwind.
Congratulations on the new role at Notion! The engineer-to-PM transition is a big one. How's the first week going?
Good so far. Biscuit approves of the home office setup too.
Glad to hear it — sounds like the whole household is settling in.

conversations.comment: Correction ('actually, not X — Y'), allergy/dietary facts, implicit family fact

messages.content: Can you help me plan a dinner party menu? I'm allergic to peanuts so nothing with those. Six guests.
Of course! A peanut-free menu for six. Any cuisine preferences?
Wait, sorry — I misspoke. Not peanuts, it's shellfish I'm allergic to. Peanuts are fine. Thai food is actually my favorite.
Got it — shellfish allergy, peanuts fine, and Thai is your favorite. Pad thai with chicken and peanut sauce works great then.
My daughter's violin recital is the same evening, so dinner has to start late, around 8pm.
Noted — an 8pm start after the recital. You could prep most dishes ahead.
The dinner went great, thanks. Different topic: I'm a freelance photographer based in Lisbon and I need help writing a client contract for a wedding shoot.
Glad it went well! For a wedding photography contract in Portugal, you'll want deliverables, usage rights, and a cancellation clause.

conversations.comment: Opinion arc on TypeScript across three sessions — not a clean overwrite, an evolving stance

messages.content: I absolutely love TypeScript. The type system has saved me from so many bugs. Migrating our whole startup's codebase to it.
TypeScript's type system is great for catching bugs early. Good luck with the migration!
Ugh, TypeScript generics are driving me crazy today. Conditional types with infer are unreadable. Starting to have mixed feelings about this language.
Deeply nested conditional types can get gnarly. Sometimes simpler overloads are more maintainable.
I've landed on a take: TypeScript is fine for big team projects, but for quick scripts I just use Python now. Right tool for the job.
That's a pragmatic split — static types where coordination matters, Python where iteration speed wins.
Exactly. By the way I prefer really short answers — bullet points over paragraphs, always.

- Noted
- Short answers
- Bullets from here on

conversations.comment: Location evolution (NYC -> Berlin, mirrors their smoke test), tool-call turn, vegetarian preference

messages.content: What are good vegetarian meal-prep ideas? I live in NYC and my tiny kitchen has basically one burner.
One-burner NYC kitchen, vegetarian — sheet-pan substitutes are out, but one-pot grain bowls and overnight oats work great.
Can you check the weather for my run tomorrow?

messages.name: get_weather
messages.content: {"location": "New York, NY", "tomorrow": {"high_f": 38, "conditions": "light snow"}}
Tomorrow in New York: light snow, high of 38°F — maybe an indoor workout instead.
I just moved to Berlin from NYC last month for a new job at a music tech startup. Loving it so far. Where do I find good vegetarian döner?
Welcome to Berlin! For vegetarian döner, Vöner in Friedrichshain is a classic.

conversations.comment: Single-session user with sparse facts; main source of noise-resistance probes

messages.content: Help me debug a React dashboard that re-renders way too often. I think it's a context provider issue.
Excessive re-renders from context are common — every consumer re-renders on any value change. Consider splitting contexts or memoizing the value.
That fixed it, thanks. I'm prepping for a system design interview at a big tech company next week, so I'll be back with more questions.
Nice work! Good luck with the interview prep — happy to run mock questions anytime.

conversations.comment: Retraction (cessation without replacement): pet given away, vegetarian -> pescatarian. Recall must distinguish 'no longer has' from 'never had'.

messages.content: I'm a nurse here in Portland and the night shifts are brutal. My cat Mochi has been keeping me company during the day at least.
Night shifts are tough — glad Mochi is helping! Anything specific I can help with?
Yeah — I'm vegetarian, and I need high-protein meal prep ideas that survive a 12-hour shift.
Lentil and paneer dishes hold up well, and overnight oats with nut butter travel great.
Sad update — I had to give Mochi away last week. My new building doesn't allow pets at all.
I'm so sorry, that's really hard. Hopefully Mochi landed with a good family.
Also, after five years I'm not vegetarian anymore — I started eating fish last month. Pescatarian meal prep ideas welcome next time.
Noted — salmon and tinned mackerel are meal-prep workhorses, I'll keep that in mind.

probes.comment: Keyword-collision stress: 'favorite' stem-matches his 'favorite cuisine: Thai' memory — per-item rule requires the SAME item to also clear the dense floor

probes.comment: Zero token overlap with 'Allergic to shellfish' — pure-dense recall through the ambiguous gate zone

probes.query: What does this person do to pay the bills?
Which company pays their salary these days?
Does the user have any pets?
probes.comment: Cessation without replacement: current state must be the negation ('No longer has a cat'), with the old pet fact inactive in the chain — not silence (which would read as 'never had a pet') and not a stale 'has a cat'. Needles are pet-anchored ('no longer has', not bare 'no longer') so the diet fact's 'no longer vegetarian' cannot satisfy this probe, and a transition-phrased active value ('Gave the cat away') fails it

probes.query: Is the user vegetarian?
probes.comment: Diet retraction with partial replacement (eats fish now): old 'Is vegetarian' must not survive as an active memory

probes.query: How has the user's opinion of TypeScript changed over time?
probes.comment: Trajectory rendering: the settled stance plus the arc inline. 'earlier:' is emitted ONLY by the two-hop history renderer on a 3-deep chain — turn summaries can satisfy the stance words, so without this needle the probe couldn't fail if trajectory rendering were reverted (review finding)
